subject: Post-call: Genexa air-gapped ops, firmware & maintenance cadence
messages:
From: Alex Rodgers <arodgers@genexa.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
Cc: Priya Mehta <priya.mehta@genexa.com>
Date: 2028-04-10T15:03:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up & clarifications from today's air-gap readiness call

Hi Soojin —

Thanks for the call earlier. Quick recap from our side and a few clarifying asks so we can progress procurement and internal approvals: 

- Current ask: on-prem sealed (air-gapped) deployment for our R&D cluster (Genexa research lab, SF).
- Expected initial capacity: 4 x inference nodes (24 A100 equiv), 1 management appliance.
- Priority: predictable offline patch cadence and a clear upgrade pathway that doesn't require outbound connectivity.

Can you confirm the following items for our security and facilities teams: 
1) Hardware compatibility: do you publish an SKU list we can cross-check against our procurement catalog?
2) Upgrade/patch mechanism: what is the offline upgrade flow (staging image, USB transfer, air-gap validation)? How often are security patches released and what is the supported rollback window?
3) Maintenance windows and remote support: we will be strictly offline during normal ops; what minimal connectivity (if any) do you require for support engagements or must all support be onsite/console-based?
4) Evidence for compliance: SOC2 artifact types, audit log export format, and any third-party penetration test reports you can share.

Attaching our network diagram and a short checklist. Happy to share a read-only inventory export if that helps.

Next step from our side: schedule a 60-minute technical workshop with your ops/field team and our infra/security owners. We are aiming for the week of Apr 17.

Thanks — Alex

--
Alex Rodgers
Head of IT Infrastructure | Genexa Therapeutics
arodgers@genexa.com | +1 415-555-0192

Attachments: Genexa_Network_Diagram.png (image), Genexa_Reqs_Checklist.xlsx (spreadsheet)

From: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>
To: Alex Rodgers <arodgers@genexa.com>
Cc: Priya Mehta <priya.mehta@genexa.com>, Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-04-10T17:22:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up & clarifications from today's air-gap readiness call

Alex —

Appreciate the clear summary and the diagram. Short answers up-front and then a proposed plan: 

1) SKU list: yes, we maintain an HW compatibility matrix. I'll attach the current compatibility PDF and call out any model-specific caveats below.
2) Offline upgrades: we support a signed image bundle that can be transferred via removable media. Standard flow: pre-stage image with a checksum on an air-gapped staging host -> offline validation -> apply during maintenance window -> KV-cache compatibility check post-upgrade. Security patches are released quarterly for critical CVEs with emergency hotfixes as needed; rollback is supported for 72 hours with a snapshot-based fallback if you maintain the pre-upgrade images.
3) Support model: normal ops with strict air-gap means we operate via on-site engineer runbook + remote support via redacted logs exchanged through an approved secure courier (we can discuss an enclave for encrypted transfer). For higher SLAs we can support a dedicated on-site engineer during the initial 30-day stabilization. No outbound call-home is required unless you opt-in for telemetry.
4) Evidence: SOC2 Type II summary, syslog export formats (JSON lines), and redacted penetration test summaries are available. I'll coordinate access to documents via our secure portal.

Proposed next steps: 
- Internal alignment: Ben, Priyom — please review the attached compatibility matrix and confirm any hardware exclusions or special firmware constraints.
- Schedule: Alex, are you okay with a working session on Apr 18 or Apr 19 (60 minutes) to walk the team through the offline upgrade demo and support handoff?

I will also surface a short checklist for procurement items (power, UPS, KVM access, removable media policy) in my follow-up.

Thanks,
Soojin

--
Soojin Lee
Technical Account Manager, Redwood Inference
soojin@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

From: Ben Carter <ben@redwood.com>
To: Soojin Lee <soojin@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom@redwood.com>
Cc: Alex Rodgers <arodgers@genexa.com>, Priya Mehta <priya.mehta@genexa.com>
Date: 2028-04-10T20:11:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up & clarifications from today's air-gap readiness call

Soojin / team —

Quick technical clarifications from the HW side after reviewing Genexa's diagram: 

- Compatibility: Genexa's stated density (4 inference nodes) is compatible with the following families in our matrix: RDX-A100v2, RDX-A30-Q, and XTR-accelerator nodes. Caveat: if Genexa wants to use smaller OEM chassis the NVMe layout must match our KV-cache persistence expectations (two mirrored NVMe per node). See attached hw-compatibility-matrix.pdf.
- Firmware/BIOS: We require access to vendor-signed firmware images for the baseboard and NICs to validate the chain-of-trust. For air-gapped customers we include a firmware staging checklist and a signed image manifest.
- Patch cadence: Our default is quarterly cumulative security bundles plus emergency hotfixes. For customers that cannot accept quarterly downtime we offer a reduced-impact rolling patch that updates one node at a time; however, that requires a spare node or can be scheduled during low-load windows.
- Rollback: snapshot-based rollback uses per-node images; we recommend keeping the pre-upgrade image and a checksum for 14 days to be safe (we can shorten to 72 hours but need signoff).
- Support: For strict air-gap we provide runbooks, an encrypted tape/USB transfer flow for logs, and optionally a 30-day on-site commissioning package (3 days onsite + 24/7 phone support to the on-site engineer).

Action items for the customer call: 
- Confirm whether Genexa can provide vendor-signed firmware images or if Redwood will stage images on their behalf.
- Confirm acceptable rollback retention period (72h vs 14d).
- Decide if they want the commissioning package (onsite engineer) for first 30 days.

--
Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
ben@redwood.com

Attachments: hw-compatibility-matrix.pdf

Alex / Priya —

Thanks for the notes. From an engagement and procurement perspective here's a short customer-facing plan we can send after you confirm the workshop time: 

1) Technical workshop (60m) — demo of offline upgrade + Q&A (deliverable: runbook draft, proposed maintenance window schedule).
2) Procurement pack — HW SKU list, power/cooling checklist, on-site commissioning options, and a one-page SOW outline for the initial 90-day stabilization (deliverable: PDF).
3) Compliance evidence handover — we will share SOC2 summary and redacted pentest report via our secure portal; please confirm required NDA level and supply contact for evidence ingestion.
4) Timeline: target 4–6 week lead time for procurement once SKUs are approved; commissioning + validation estimated at 2 weeks on-site.

Please confirm preferred workshop slot (Apr 18 or Apr 19) and who from your side will attend (security, facilities, procurement). I will open a HubSpot activity and attach the procurement pack and DocuSign link when the workshop is scheduled: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/67890

If you want, we can also draft a short appendix describing the offline log transfer flow so your security team can review desktop-to-courier process beforehand.

Best —
Priyom
